top_signals.title: Anthropic IPO Shutout Sends Asia’s Investors Into Proxy Bets
top_signals.summary: For much of Asia, getting a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering may prove nearly impossible. That’s pushing investors toward a collection of proxies, from the Claude maker’s listed shareholders to crypto derivatives and semiconductor stocks.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: RBNZ Governor Says Further Rate Increases Highly Likely
top_signals.summary: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman says further OCR increases are highly likely at coming meetings after policymakers voted 4-3 to leave rates unchanged. She points to anchored inflation expectations, subdued wage growth and weak domestic demand. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Europe’s debt stress is hitting corporate borrowing costs. Goldman flags who’s vulnerable
top_signals.summary: Sovereign debt pressure and heavy bond issuance are raising European corporate borrowing costs, squeezing companies with weaker balance sheets, Goldman said.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: UBS CEO Ermotti on Earnings, Cost Savings, Capital Return
top_signals.summary: UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti speaks to Bloomberg's Stephen Carroll after the lender posted third-quarter profit broadly in line with expectations, with a surge in client inflows potentially buoying the outlook for the global wealth manager. The Zurich-based bank said net income in the three months through September was $2.69 billion, while net new assets in the wealth unit came in at $55.1 billion, led by Asia Pacific and the Americas. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Healey to Scrap UK’s Standing Charges on Gas Bills
top_signals.summary: Standing charges on gas bills will be scrapped for millions of British households as soon as next year, Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will announce today.
